causal_identification_attacks: The cloned-state intervention is not a true causal experiment on the persistent learning process because it only tests a one-step update. The longitudinal claim—that repeated winner-only updates cause weaker frozen skill than L/L—requires a different causal estimand that the one-step clone design cannot identify. The dossier acknowledges this but the paper must not conflate the two.

The precommitted rollout-0 arm is not a valid counterfactual for 'what the learner would have seen without winner selection' because rollout-0 is still generated under the same search policy and skill state. It is a different observation kernel, not a no-censoring baseline. The identity V_pre = 1-p is a modeling assumption about what the learner would see, not an observed quantity.

The acting invariance validator requires that all high-K arms serve the exact same winner. This is only possible if the winner selection is deterministic given the pool. Any stochasticity in the verifier or selector breaks the exact-same-pool claim and confounds the projection effect with acting differences.

The prospective prediction F3 is vulnerable to outcome-driven family selection. If the held-out families are chosen after seeing which families show large Gamma or delta in development, the prediction is not prospective. The dossier requires pre-outcome freezing, but the audit does not specify a mechanism to prevent post-hoc family redefinition.

The family overlap problem is not solved by the dossier. The mutually exclusive partition Z of mixed pools is asserted as necessary but no operational rule is given for assigning a mixed pool with multiple failure types to a single family. Without this, the sum over z of Pr(M, Z=z) × delta_z is not identified.

The delta_z estimand requires a fixed updater and a fixed future task distribution. If the updater's behavior depends on the order of updates or the specific contrast packet format, delta_z is not a stable property of the failure family but an artifact of the particular updater implementation. The paper must either fix the updater and report delta_z as conditional on it, or acknowledge that the mechanism does not generalize across updaters.
review.decisive_kill_experiment: The cloned-state exact-same-pool projection-null experiment (F2). Take one fixed pre-update skill state S, one task batch, one exact K-pool T_K, one acting winner, one updater, one verifier, one update seed. Clone S into arms that differ only in g(T_K): winner-only vs. precommitted rollout-0 vs. rejected-witness vs. contrast packet. Then freeze all skills and evaluate on a common held-out probe with K=1. If changing g(T_K) produces no directional difference in future frozen skill J(U(S,g(T_K))) in the predicted direction, the central mechanism is dead regardless of any longitudinal or prospective results. This single experiment isolates the entire causal claim: that the learning projection, not the acting projection or compute amount, drives persistent skill quality.

deeper_scientific_object.object: Outcome-dependent observation kernels in sequential decision-feedback loops, where the deployed policy determines which generated outcomes become visible to a persistent learner. This subsumes Search-Projection Censoring as a special case where the deployed policy is a best-of-K verifier-selected winner and the learner is an external skill updater. It also subsumes selective labels, performative prediction, and DAgger as instances of the same structure: a decision rule induces an observation distribution that feeds back into future behavior.
deeper_scientific_object.why_deeper: The R17 object is a specific instantiation of a more general phenomenon: any system that generates multiple candidate outcomes and then selects one for deployment creates a missing-not-at-random observation process for any learner that only sees the deployed outcome. The deeper object is the coupling between the selection rule and the learner's observation kernel, of which winner-only best-of-K is one parametric case. This would unify R17 with RLVR pass@k inversion, selective labels, and performative prediction under a single formal object: the mapping from deployment policy to learner-visible distribution and its fixed points.

review.formula_or_mechanism_that_is_pretty_but_: The Gamma_K(p_z) × delta_z factorization is currently attractive but scientifically underidentified. The identity Gamma_K is exact, but delta_z = 'expected future gain from failure/contrast evidence minus expected future gain from served-success evidence' is not a measurable quantity without a precommitted, mutually exclusive failure-family partition and a fixed updater. The dossier itself admits overlapping post-hoc failure tags cannot be summed. Until delta_z is operationally defined via a frozen disjoint partition and a specific updater, the product is a tautological decomposition of an effect into 'how much was censored' times 'how valuable the censored evidence was', with the second factor free to absorb any residual. The continuous-verifier layer-cake extension is mathematically valid but adds no empirical content beyond the binary case unless a threshold policy is actually used.
review.irreducible_novelty: The exact rescue-censoring identity A_K - A_1 = V_pre - V_win = Gamma_K(Q) = Pr(Y_1=0, max_i Y_i=1), which holds without independence or exchangeability assumptions, together with the cloned-state exact-same-pool intervention that changes only the learning projection g(T_K) while holding the acting winner fixed. This is a precise order-statistic/coupling identity about how acting selection changes the updater-visible experience distribution, not a general claim that failures are useful or that search can harm learning.

method_collision_assessment.SkillCAT: SkillCAT is a direct method collision for the CADP contrast packet. It already does same-task multi-seed success/failure pairing, first-divergence extraction, contrastive skill editing, and replay validation in an external persistent-skill pipeline. CADP cannot claim novelty for any of these components. The only residual is the serving-time endogenous censoring mechanism and the exact identity, which SkillCAT does not study. If the paper's contribution is 'use success/failure contrast to update a skill', it is not novel. If the contribution is 'serving-time winner selection endogenously removes the failure evidence that SkillCAT-style methods would use', that is a different and potentially novel claim, but it requires the causal intervention to establish.
method_collision_assessment.TopoCurate: TopoCurate is a direct representation/selection collision. It already argues that outcome-based filtering ignores interaction dynamics and uses branch/error topology to select training data. The R17 claim that winner-only projection discards useful structure is not novel. The residual is the specific serving-time best-of-K selection mechanism and the exact identity, which TopoCurate does not address. However, the paper must not frame its contribution as 'success filtering loses information' because TopoCurate already established that.
other: Rethinking Self-Evolving Agent Skills (arXiv:2608.02636) already established that failure feedback is essential for skill evolution and that test-time scaling differs from persistent skill improvement. The R17 claim that failures matter is not novel. The residual is the endogenous censoring mechanism, not the value of failure feedback.

Search-E1, Sibling-Guided Credit Distillation, Outcome-Verified Comparative Self-Distillation, and SKILL-KD already use sibling trajectories, success/failure divergence, and contrastive distillation. R17 cannot claim novelty for sibling contrast or first-divergence extraction.

Do Not Waste Your Rollouts and TSR already establish that search experience can be recycled into training. The claim that search can teach more is already established. R17 must condition its claim on the learning projection, not on search budget.

SkillOpt and SkillHEX already establish bounded validation-gated skill editing, rejected-edit memory, and diagnostic evidence for skill revision. R17 cannot claim novelty for the optimizer feature bundle.

Selective labels, performative prediction, and DAgger are mature conceptual reductions. R17 is a specialized instance of these frameworks. The paper must acknowledge this and not claim to discover a new general phenomenon.

review.recommendation: REVISE_AND_NARROW. The paper should be reframed as a mechanism-level causal study of serving-induced selective trajectory logging in persistent self-evolution, with the exact rescue-censoring identity as a definitional tool, not a theorem. The CADP method should be demoted to a simple Rejected-Witness baseline unless the contrast packet beats it. The paper must not claim novelty for success/failure pairing, first divergence, bounded editing, replay validation, or rejected-edit memory. The decisive F2 cloned-state projection-null experiment must pass before any longitudinal or prospective claims are made. If SkillCAT-style contrast explains the full effect without the serving-selection causal chain, the paper should be reduced to an application or stopped.
review.single_sentence_verdict: The paper has a narrow but potentially real mechanism-level novelty—serving-time winner selection endogenously censoring diagnostic failures from a persistent updater—but it is currently buried under method components that are already published, and the central causal claim is only testable through a single decisive cloned-state projection-null experiment that has not been run.
review.strongest_direct_reduction: TopoCurate (arXiv:2603.01714) is the strongest direct reduction. It already argues that outcome-based filtering of successful trajectories ignores interaction dynamics, projects multiple same-task trials into a semantic quotient topology containing effective and failure branches, and uses branch/error structure to select training data. This preempts the general claim that winner-only selection discards useful branch structure. The residual R17 claim must be the serving-time endogenous censoring mechanism and the exact identity, not the general 'success filtering loses information' statement.
theory_attacks: The independence-free identity A_K - A_1 = Pr(Y_1=0, max_i Y_i=1) is a trivial algebraic rearrangement: A_K - A_1 = E[max_i Y_i - Y_1] = Pr(Y_1=0, max_i Y_i=1) for binary Y_i. It is not a scientific discovery; it is a definition of the rescue-censoring event. The paper must not present this as a theorem with explanatory power.

The i.i.d. Bernoulli specialization Gamma_K(p) = (1-p) - (1-p)^K and its maximizer p*(K) = 1 - K^(-1/(K-1)) are elementary order-statistic calculations. The intermediate-difficulty peak is a property of the binomial model, not an empirical law. Any deviation from i.i.d. (which the dossier admits is likely) destroys the peak location and the one-parameter curve.

The correlated-rollout prediction that heterogeneity reduces Gamma_K relative to the i.i.d. curve is a Jensen's inequality observation about concavity of (1-theta) - (1-theta)^K. It is mathematically true but provides no quantitative prediction without a model of the heterogeneity distribution.

The continuous-verifier layer-cake identity E[max_i R_i - R_1] = integral of [V_pre(t) - V_win(t)] dt is a standard layer-cake representation. It does not strengthen the scientific claim; it merely restates the binary identity at every threshold. The paper should not imply this is a substantive extension.

The information-theoretic statement I(Z; g_win(T_K)) <= I(Z; T_K) is a direct consequence of the data-processing inequality for deterministic coarsening. It is true but vacuous as a scientific claim: it says a richer observation has weakly more information for a Bayes-optimal learner, which the dossier itself admits does not apply to a fixed LLM updater. This should be removed or explicitly labeled as non-contributing intuition.

The Gamma × delta factorization is exact only under the gated-projection construction where the alternative projection equals winner-only outside the mixed event M. This is a tautological decomposition: any effect of changing the projection can be written as Pr(M) × E[effect | M]. The scientific content is entirely in whether delta_z is positive and predictable, which is an empirical claim about the updater, not a theoretical result.
review.thesis_reduction_verdict: The thesis is partially reducible but not fully reducible. The broad claim that winner/success filtering discards useful failure structure is already established by TopoCurate and Rethinking Self-Evolving Agent Skills. The specific mechanism—serving-time best-of-K selection endogenously censoring diagnostic failures from an external persistent updater, with an exact acting-gain/failure-visibility identity—is not directly reduced by any cited work.
